questions.question: How comfortable are you writing graph algorithms from memory right now?
questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether the cheat sheet includes full implementation templates, skeleton reminders, or only pattern-to-algorithm mappings.

options.label: Can write BFS/DFS/Dijkstra cold
options.implication: Cheat sheet focuses on pattern recognition tables, complexity summaries, and edge-case checklists — no boilerplate code.

options.label: Know the logic but forget syntax details
options.implication: Includes minimal, copy-pasteable templates for each algorithm (initialization, loop structure, return) plus pattern triggers.

options.label: Need a refresher on the algorithms themselves
options.implication: Adds a one-page refresher per algorithm (invariant, key variables, termination) before the pattern-mapping section.

questions.default_label: Know the logic but forget syntax details

questions.question: What does "interview-ready" look like for you?
questions.why_it_matters: Changes the artifact from a pure recognition guide to an implementation drill sheet or a verbal-explanation crib.

options.label: Implement from scratch in 20–25 min
options.implication: Full templates with boilerplate, common bug annotations, and timed practice prompts for each pattern.

options.label: Modify a given starter implementation
options.implication: Focuses on the delta: which lines change per variant, edge-case guards, and complexity trade-off notes.

options.label: Explain approach and complexity verbally
options.implication: Pattern → algorithm mapping, one-sentence invariant per algorithm, complexity table, and follow-up question cues.
